answer: The ocean decay curve is applied at each close, lantern records the drop, and jetty recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 210 aliases cost 285 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
